title: ASR Evaluation: WER & CER
interviewAnswer: Word Error Rate counts substitutions, deletions and insertions relative to reference word count. It is interpretable but can hide semantic differences and depends on text normalization conventions.
why: ASR Evaluation: WER & CER appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Word Error Rate counts substitutions, deletions and insertions relative to reference word count. It is interpretable but can hide semantic differences and depends on text normalization conventions. Normalize references/hypotheses consistently. Slice by accent/noise/domain. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A transcript with one substitution and one deletion over 20 words has WER 10%.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does ASR Evaluation: WER & CER make?
How would you validate or debug ASR Evaluation: WER & CER in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
